subject: Addendum: 3 goal-pinned Codex automations (D/E/F), permission-stall audit applied to all 6 new loops, one fire-to-receipt witness test proving the mechanism closes end-to-end
highest_value_findings: All 6 pre-existing ACTIVE Codex automations and all 6 new ones use ONLY shell/git/curl/file-I-O, zero MCP tool calls -- grepped verbatim, confirmed. This is why the L_SCHEDULER_FIRES_PERMISSION_STALLS class observed on Antigravity (per-conversation MCP consent dialog blocking every fire) has never manifested in this Codex install's history, and the 6 new loops were deliberately built the same way rather than risk it.

Whether Codex's headless scheduler bypasses the interactive on-request approval gate for an MCP tool call specifically remains UNKNOWN -- honestly unresolved, not assumed safe. What IS verified: config.toml approval_policy=on-request + sandbox_mode=workspace-write + C:\Dev trust_level=trusted, and empirically Fenrir/Garmr complete network+file operations unattended across dozens of cycles -- strong evidence for bash-only loops, no evidence either way for MCP-calling loops (because none exist to test).

Ground-truthed the LOGO->100APPS pipeline via live curl: exactly 1 of 25 probed demoNN-handpiano.pages.dev slots is live (demo01 only). Landed this as a real witness-test receipt in state/ssot/goal_spatial_shipping.jsonl, not a placeholder -- proves the fire-to-receipt mechanism closes end-to-end for at least one of the 6 new loops, satisfying the addendum's ship-gate requirement.

state/ssot/quorum_syntheses.jsonl (the canonical source hfo-codex-goal-cross-family-quorum-daily was asked to read) does not exist yet -- created empty this session; the loop's real signal today would come from state/ssot/valkyrie_votes_*.jsonl's existing 'family' field until a canonical quorum_syntheses producer exists.
verifier_result: Live curl (25 requests) for the spatial-shipping witness test, landed and read back. Grepped all 12 automation.toml prompts (6 pre-existing + 6 new) for MCP/plugin references -- zero true positives (one false-positive substring match in Garmr's own FORBIDDEN list, verified by reading surrounding context). Read C:/Users/tommy/.codex/config.toml verbatim for approval_policy/sandbox_mode/trust_level. Validated all 6 new TOML files with python tomllib and confirmed status=PAUSED on every one. 2 more scoped git commits pushed and confirmed via git log + git push remote output.
remaining_risk: The core open question (does Codex's scheduler stall on an MCP consent dialog the same way Antigravity does) is NOT resolved by this session -- it is sidestepped by construction (6 new loops call zero MCP tools) rather than answered. If the operator later wants an MCP-calling Codex loop, that question must be tested for real before trusting it to run unattended.

hfo-codex-goal-cross-family-quorum-daily's 'major action' classification is a keyword heuristic (immunize/canon/seal/succession/promotion/boundary_primitive/hmac substring match on SIGRUN_P4.jsonl rows), not a formal schema tag -- will produce false positives/negatives until a real major-action tag exists.

hfo-codex-goal-income-hunt-4h's income-tag matching falls back to a weak substring heuristic on task title/objective if no explicit goal/tags field exists -- task_queue.jsonl's current single row has neither, so this loop's first real cycle would likely find zero income-tagged work and immediately queue its own first action, which is intended behavior but untested against a live fire.
honest_flaw: The witness test proves ONE of the 6 new loops (goal-spatial-shipping) closes end-to-end when its exact logic is run manually; it does not prove the other 5, and it does not prove any of the 6 will behave identically when actually fired by Codex's real scheduler rather than rehearsed by a Claude session. That gap is named explicitly in the plan doc's pre-authorization section, not hidden.
next_safe_action: Operator arms hfo-codex-goal-spatial-factory-shipping-daily FIRST (lowest risk, already witness-tested, pure read-only curl) and checks state/ssot/goal_spatial_shipping.jsonl for a second row with executor=codex_gpt within 24h -- that single observation answers the open MCP-stall question empirically for at least the bash-only loop class, before arming the other 5.
